newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK POLICE CLASH AT CANADIAN TVX GOLD MINE.
newsitem.headline: GREEK POLICE CLASH AT CANADIAN TVX GOLD MINE.

text.p: Riot police clashed with local residents blockading a main access road to Canada's TVX Gold operations in northern Greece, and a number of people were injured and arrested, local officials said.

"There are violent clashes taking place now. There are a number of injured and some, including local officials, have been arrested," George Kostis, president of nearby Varvara village, told Flash radio.
TVX Gold Hellas, the Greek subsidiary, threatened last night to stop work and to stop paying wages to 650 workers at the TVX operation from next week unless the access road was opened.
Several Athens radio stations reported clashes between police and residents or between TVX employees and residents, saying several people had been injured.
Police in the area were out of contact and unable to confirm or give details of the incident.

Local residents of Varvara and nearby Olympiada have blocked the main road since TVX bought the mine last December, saying a planned gold processing plant would damage the environment and the tourist industry. --Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
